areas.name: Verify, messages and the assertion analyzers
Mock shapes and the shape sweep
Test registration and the runner process

decisions.question: What a failure message shows, and which exception surfaces, when formatting a captured value or an interpolated message hole throws or changes state.
Which setup wins when typed and NSubstitute-style setups, or overlapping matchers, configure the same call.

Which argument equality decides recursive mock identity, what a recursive member returns after its parent is reconfigured, and whether the default returned at the depth limit is a contract tests may rely on.
Which orderings of pending setups, matchers and checks are legal across awaits, child tasks and parallel calls.
The order of failures when a scope listener, a class scope or the assembly scope fails during cleanup, and when cancellation arrives during cleanup.
Whether the scope's exception keeps the exception the test threw, which check.md says it replaces outside VerificationGlue.Tests.
How a scope collects Check failures from child tasks that run in parallel, and in what order it reports them.
What a test reports when a parameter provider or the container throws while resolving a parameter.
What happens when an Arg.Is predicate throws, and the state of the next mock operation after any misuse failure.
Whether a type nested in a generic type whose type arguments come from an extern-aliased assembly gets a VGM0001 refusal or is supported.

scenarios.contract: Verify returns without effect when the condition is true.
Without the generator, a false condition throws VerifyException with 'Verify failed: ' and the condition's source text, and no shape line, file or line.
With the generator, a failure gives the shape line for the condition and the call's file, relative to the project, and line.
dimensions: expression shape: each row of the shape table

scenarios.contract: A call written on several lines reports the line where it starts, and an operand written on several lines gives no shape line.
A passing call neither throws nor formats its message, and the holes of an interpolated message run only when the condition is false.
dimensions: execution path: generator absent, interceptor, tier 3 copy

scenarios.contract: An interpolated message appears in the failure before the file and line.
A method of another type named Verify is neither intercepted nor analyzed.
Verify at tiers 1 and 2 keeps C# evaluation: each part of the condition runs once, in order, with short-circuiting, and an exception from the condition propagates unchanged.
dimensions: outcome: pass, failure, expression exception, cancellation
scenarios.constraints: Tier 2 runs in the fixed-seed run. Tier 1 runs in the run with the generator off, which must match plain C# in everything but the tier.

scenarios.contract: Each message on the messages page matches a fresh run of its sample.
A Native AOT build reports the same message, file and line as a JIT build.
scenarios.constraints: Checked on linux-x64 only, in the build job.

scenarios.contract: VG0002 warns about a constant condition, and VG0003 about a condition with a side effect. Plain conditions report nothing.
VG0004 warns about an exact == or != comparison of float or double values.

A captured value whose ToString throws or changes state still gives a failure that reports the original condition. The value shows a placeholder that names the formatting exception's type, and ToString runs once, on the failure path.

An interpolated message hole whose value throws while it is formatted does not hide the assertion failure. The hole shows a placeholder that names the formatting exception's type. A hole expression that throws surfaces its own exception, because C# evaluates it at the call site.
dimensions: execution path: generator absent, tier 3 copy
hole: plain, alignment, format, alignment and format

scenarios.contract: Every diagnostic has a page with the standard sections, and each descriptor links to it.
A failed Check records the failure in the current scope and lets the code after it run.
When the scope ends, it throws one VerifyException that gives the count and lists every failed Check in order.
With no open scope, Check throws at once, as Verify does.
A Check in a static constructor, a finalizer or a module initializer runs where no scope can be open.

outcome.detail: VG0007 warns at the call. At run time Check throws at once, as with no scope.

scenarios.contract: In a method that tier 3 rewrites, each failed Check lists its values.
In VerificationGlue.Tests, Check needs no setup, and its failures are reported with the test that made them.
Check with VerifyScope.Begin() works the same in xunit, NUnit, MSTest and TUnit.
A scope with no failures ends without throwing and leaves no current scope.
A scope begun inside another reports its own failures when it ends, and the outer scope becomes current again.
The scope flows with async and await, so a Check in an awaited method reports to the caller's scope.
Ending a scope twice reports its failures once.
Verify inside a scope still throws at the first failure.

When a test outside VerificationGlue.Tests throws after failed checks, the scope's exception keeps the exception the test threw as its InnerException. An exception the test caught before the scope ended is not kept.
scenarios.constraints: Not under Native AOT, where Marshal.GetExceptionPointers is not supported and the scope's exception has no InnerException.

scenarios.contract: Check failures from child tasks that run in parallel inside one scope are all reported. Their order is not part of the contract.
dimensions: children: threads started at once, tasks awaited together

scenarios.contract: Throws<T> returns the exception the action throws, also when it derives from T.
Throws<T> fails with 'no exception was thrown' when the action throws nothing.
Throws<T> fails on an exception that is not a T, names its type and message, and keeps it as the InnerException.
ThrowsAsync<T> awaits the action and returns its exception, or fails when it throws nothing.
ThrowsAsync<T> fails on an exception that is not a T, as Throws<T> does, including an exception the action throws before it returns a task and a cancelled task.
dimensions: outcome: different exception, synchronous throw, cancellation

scenarios.contract: A Throws or ThrowsAsync failure reports the shape line 'expected call to throw T' with the file and line, and a type parameter T names the type at run time.
Throws in a method that tier 3 rewrites keeps its tier 2 message.
An eligible [Verify] method gets a __Verified copy, and each direct call, including an extension call, runs the copy.
A call to an eligible method from inside another copy calls the copy.
In the copy each part of the condition runs once, in the original order, and nothing runs a second time to build the message.
A passing check in the copy does not allocate, and constants and literals are not captured.
Rewriting keeps statement structure: an embedded statement gets braces, an out variable stays in scope after the call, and an await stays in the condition.
A part on the side of &&, ||, ?: or ?? that did not run is not evaluated and shows <not evaluated>.
A ref struct value, a pointer, or the receiver of a call on a mutable struct is not captured.

outcome.detail: The message shows <unavailable> for the part, and VG0006 reports it as information.

scenarios.contract: A part whose type has no name is declared from the part, and one that declares a variable is reported as text only.
A failure in the copy lists the captured values, and Because adds its reason.
.Because or .WithMessage after a Verify that tier 3 does not rewrite never runs.

outcome.detail: VG0001 warns at the chained call. The failure message has no reason.

scenarios.contract: A [Verify] method in a type that is not partial is not rewritten.

outcome.detail: VG0005 warns, with a code fix that makes each containing type partial. The method keeps tier 2 messages.

scenarios.contract: A [Verify] method whose file declares a file type is not rewritten.

outcome.detail: VG0008 warns. The method keeps tier 2 messages.

scenarios.contract: A [Verify] method with syntax errors is not copied.

outcome.detail: No copy is written and the method keeps tier 2 messages. Other generators see WillRewrite as false.

scenarios.contract: A [Verify] method that is generic, virtual, abstract, override or extern, returns by reference, is an instance method of a struct, has #if directives, sits in a generic, private or protected type, or uses a private nested, pointer or dynamic type in its signature is not rewritten.

outcome.detail: No copy is written, no diagnostic is reported, and the method keeps tier 2 messages.

scenarios.contract: A Verify or Check inside a lambda or a local function in a copy keeps its tier 2 message.

outcome.detail: The call keeps its tier 2 message.

scenarios.contract: The original method still gives tier 2 messages, so a framework that calls a [Verify] test through reflection gets tier 2.
The copy maps to the original file and line, passes the original name to CallerMemberName, and binds with the using aliases and extension methods of its file.
With VerificationGlueRewrite off, no copy or redirect is written.
Other generators see WillRewrite true exactly when a copy exists, and each runner call binds and runs.
A [VerifyTest] method runs its copy, because the runner calls it directly and only when WillRewrite is true.
Mock.Of<T>() creates a mock whose unconfigured members return auto-values.
Every call is recorded with its arguments, including 1,000 parallel calls.
Returns answers calls whose arguments match and leaves other calls unconfigured.
Returns with several values answers each in turn and then repeats the last. Matching calls share one sequence, and a new setup replaces it.
A Returns factory runs on each call, reads the arguments through CallInfo, and can set an out argument. A factory that throws makes the call throw.
Throws makes matching calls throw, on void members too.
When(...).Do(...) runs its callback on each matching call, and the call that selects the member is not recorded.
The last setup for a call wins, whether it is exact or uses Arg.Any.
The call inside a setup is not a received call, in either setup style.
A setup call runs the response set up before it, as in NSubstitute.
A property returns the value set on it, a set after Returns wins, and Returns null on a string member wins over the empty-string auto-value.
Properties, indexers, generic methods and out parameters take setups in both styles, and a generic method matches its type argument.
Two mocks of one interface share no configuration and no recorded calls.
The typed surface and the NSubstitute style drive the same mock, and Throws, Does and sequences apply to matching calls in the typed surface.
Arg.Any<T>() matches every value including null, Arg.Is matches by predicate or by value, and other arguments must be equal.
A matcher applies to the argument it is written at, also when another argument holds the default value.
An array argument, params or not, matches an array with equal elements.
Typed matchers Arg<T>.Any() and Arg<T>.Is(...) match by predicate or value, a plain value matches exactly, and a default argument matches the default value.
A matcher on an indexer argument matches.
Arg.Any<T>() stands in for an out or ref argument, and a Returns factory sets it through its index.
An Arg matcher stored in a local has no position.

outcome.detail: VGM0002 warns. At run time the matcher takes the first argument that holds the default value, as NSubstitute does.

scenarios.contract: An NSubstitute-style matcher passed to the typed Setup() or Calls() surface would match only the default value.

outcome.detail: VGM0002 is reported as an error and the build fails.

scenarios.contract: An Arg.Is predicate that throws during matching does not corrupt the mock.
Received passes for a call that was made and fails with the expected call and the calls received.
Received with a count and DidNotReceive fail on the wrong count.
Received checks property reads and writes.
A Received or DidNotReceive check is not recorded as a call.
Calls() counts the matching calls, and a failed Verify on the count lists up to 10 calls the member received.
Received, DidNotReceive and Calls() take the same matchers as setups.
Verification does not consume response sequences, and repeating a check gives the same result.
Raise.Event invokes the handlers with the arguments, and with no handler adds none and records no call.
Returns on a Task<T> or ValueTask<T> member wraps a T in a completed task, and also takes a task.
dimensions: async result: Task, Task<T>, ValueTask, ValueTask<T>

scenarios.contract: An unconfigured async member returns a completed task holding the auto-value of T.
A faulted task fails the await, and Throws makes the call itself throw before there is a task.
A cancelled task passed to Returns cancels the await.
The link between a mock call and its Returns survives an await in the argument, also in 200 parallel setups.
Each documented difference from NSubstitute is intended and listed on the differences page, and every other compared case behaves the same.
A child task starts with its parent's last call, its own calls stay in the child, and a setup finished in a child task applies.
A matcher abandoned in a child task does not reach the parent, and one abandoned in the same flow fails the next call it cannot fit.
A call from another thread while Received waits for its arguments is recorded and not checked.
Every legal interleaving of setups, matchers and checks across awaits, child tasks and parallel operations gives the observations the async context rules declare.
dimensions: context: sequential, awaits, child tasks, parallel, abandoned setup state

scenarios.contract: Returns or Throws with no mock call before it in the async flow cannot attach to a call.

outcome.detail: VGM0005 warns at build. At run time the setup throws MockSetupException saying no mock call came before it, and clears the flow's queued matchers, pending check and pending raise, as every misuse failure does.

scenarios.contract: Returns on a value that is not a mock call, a setup through a local, and a mock call inside the argument of Returns apply to the last mock call in the flow.

outcome.detail: VGM0005 warns where the value is not a mock call. At run time the setup applies to the last mock call in the same async flow, as NSubstitute does.

scenarios.contract: An unconfigured member that returns an interface returns a mock, created on the first call and returned again later, which both styles can set up.
A recursive member with parameters keeps one mock for each set of arguments.
A configured recursive member returns its value and not a mock, and a Received or DidNotReceive check creates no mock.
A recursive member that returns Task<T> or ValueTask<T> returns a completed task with default, and an interface in a System namespace gets no recursive mock.

outcome.detail: The member returns a completed task with default, or default for a System interface.

scenarios.contract: The generator writes recursive mocks up to VerificationGlueMocksRecursionDepth steps from each mocked type, default 2 and 0 for off, and a type named at Mock.Of<T>() starts its own walk.
A member of a mock at the recursion depth returns default instead of a mock.

outcome.detail: The member returns default, and VGM0007 reports it as information where the walk starts.

scenarios.contract: A [Mock] attribute, or an attribute named in VerificationGlueMockAttribute, marks a mock. Other attributes mark nothing.
MockRegistry creates a mock for a type named in a [Mock] attribute or in [assembly: GenerateMock], and a generic helper can create it.
Mock.Of<T>() in a generic helper reaches a type that no call site, [Mock] attribute or GenerateMock names.

outcome.detail: VGM0004 warns at build. At run time Mock.Of<T>() throws with a message that names the fix.

scenarios.contract: Mocks work in xunit, NUnit, MSTest and TUnit, created by hand and as [Mock] parameters.
A mock is regenerated when its interface changes, here or in a referenced project or DLL, and not on unrelated edits, so it never goes stale.

A mock compiles for inherited interfaces, overlapping names, overloads, generic constraints, nullability, properties, indexers, events, supported parameter modifiers, obsolete types, extern aliases and InternalsVisibleTo. Created through Mock.Of<T>(), a [Mock] parameter, MockRegistry.Create(Type) and a generic helper, it can be set up, called and checked.
dimensions: creation: Mock.Of<T>(), [Mock] parameter, MockRegistry.Create(Type), generic helper with GenerateMock
scenarios.constraints: A type marked [Obsolete(error: true)] has no [Mock] parameter or GenerateMock, because C# lets only obsolete code name it.

scenarios.contract: Every interface in the pinned sweep of the BCL and the top 100 packages either compiles or is refused with VGM0001, and keeps the outcome pinned for it. A change of outcome or of the swept set fails the sweep.
scenarios.constraints: The sweep calls MockModelBuilder and MockEmitter directly, not the public generator.

scenarios.contract: An interface with a static abstract member, directly or through a base interface, cannot be mocked.

outcome.detail: VGM0001 error naming the static abstract member, at each place that names the type. No mock is generated.

scenarios.contract: An interface with an abstract member the test project cannot see cannot be mocked.

outcome.detail: VGM0001 error naming the member that is not accessible.

scenarios.contract: An interface with pointer members in a project without AllowUnsafeBlocks cannot be mocked.

outcome.detail: VGM0001 error saying the members need AllowUnsafeBlocks.

scenarios.contract: A struct, a sealed or static class, a class before class mocks ship, a type the project cannot access, and an open generic type in GenerateMock cannot be mocked.

outcome.detail: VGM0001 error naming the reason, at the Mock.Of<T>() call, the [Mock] attribute or the GenerateMock attribute.

scenarios.contract: A member with a ref struct or pointer parameter, return value or property is implemented, and the rest of the mock works.

outcome.detail: VGM0003 warns where the mock is named. Calling the member throws NotSupportedException.

scenarios.contract: An event whose delegate takes a ref struct accepts handlers.

outcome.detail: Adding and removing handlers works. Raising the event throws NotSupportedException.

scenarios.contract: An open generic interface whose type parameter allows ref struct is mocked without the anti-constraint.

outcome.detail: A mock closed over a ref struct reports VGM0003 on each member that uses the type parameter.

scenarios.contract: A type nested in a generic type whose type arguments come from an extern-aliased assembly cannot be mocked, and neither can an interface whose members name such a type.

outcome.detail: VGM0001 error with its own reason, naming the nested type. A nested type whose outer type is aliased and whose type arguments are not is mocked.

scenarios.contract: Each test and constructor parameter comes from the first source with a value: a parameter-level provider, then providers on the method, class and assembly, then the container, then built-in values, then the default value.
A provider that returns false passes the parameter to the next source.
A parameter with no value fails the test with a message that names the parameter and every source tried.
A parameter provider or container that throws while resolving a parameter fails only that test with a message that names the parameter and the source, the test body does not run, and cleanup runs.
dimensions: source: provider on the parameter, provider on the class for a constructor parameter, the container

scenarios.contract: The runner uses the accessible constructor with the most parameters and resolves them in the same order as test parameters.
[Mock] parameters of the same type and key share one mock within a test, so the constructor, the method and the container see the same instance.
CancellationToken is cancelled when the run is cancelled, TestContext holds the test ID, attributes, scope and container, and ITestOutput lines reach the test's result.
When the container returns the test class, the runner uses that instance and leaves its disposal to the container.
Data rows with [Row] are planned and not shipped.

outcome.detail: There is no [Row] attribute. A generic test method, which would need rows, reports VGT0004 and is not registered.

scenarios.contract: A test with [Mock] parameters under a shared container whose bootstrap does not support child overrides would not see its mocks.

outcome.detail: VGT0008 warns at build. At run time the test fails before its body runs.

scenarios.contract: A mock or listener override reaches the system under test, and each test gets its own mock in its own child container.
Each test runs setup, body and cleanup in the documented order, with middleware around class creation and the test.
A scope is created when its first selected test starts, so a test that a filter leaves out creates nothing.
A class container is shared by its class and disposed after its last test, and an assembly container is shared across classes and disposed last.
Each test-scoped test builds and disposes its own container.
Each instance has one owner that disposes it exactly once: the container for what it creates, and the runner for a test class it created.
An override, such as a [Mock] parameter's mock, belongs to whoever added it, and the container does not dispose it.
Cleanup runs every step when one fails, and the test keeps every failure in the order it happened.
A failed Check or a cleanup failure fails a test that otherwise passed, and a later test starts with no failed checks.
A class or assembly scope that fails to dispose is reported as a failed node of its own.
An attribute constructor that throws fails only the tests of the scope that owns it, and other classes still run.
A class or assembly container that fails to build fails each test that uses it with the scope named, and is not built again.
When the run is cancelled during setup, the runner disposes what setup created and starts no more tests.

Failure or cancellation injected at scope creation, container construction, middleware entry, class construction, parameter resolution, the body, middleware exit or disposal, for each scope level, keeps ownership, cleanup and reporting.
Each retry attempt runs in a new process with fresh static state, scopes and container, and disposes its own.
A later test inherits no failed checks, mock state, pending matchers or test context from an earlier one.
The runner discovers every registered test.
The executable, dotnet run and dotnet test run only the tests that --filter-uid selects.
A run with a failed test exits with 2, and a TRX report records each outcome.
dotnet test without the Microsoft.Testing.Platform runner selected in global.json cannot run a VerificationGlue.Tests project.

outcome.detail: VGT1001 build error before the VSTest target runs.

scenarios.contract: A [VerifyTest] method the runner cannot call is not registered and does not run.

outcome.detail: VGT0004 warning naming the reason, and no registration.

dimensions: reason: each row of the VGT0004 table
interface method: abstract, default body, static

scenarios.contract: Two tests with the same test ID cannot both be registered.

outcome.detail: VGT0001 error on each method that shares the ID.

scenarios.contract: An attribute that the generated registration cannot write is left out of TestContext.Attributes.

outcome.detail: VGT0006 warns with the reason, and the test runs without the attribute.

dimensions: reason: each row of the VGT0006 table
scenarios.constraints: A named argument cannot be the reason. C# accepts only a public field or a public read-write property as a named argument (CS0617), and the registration can set any such member.

scenarios.contract: A public test returning void, Task or ValueTask, static or instance, synchronous or async, is registered and runs, with its attributes in TestContext.
The packed packages build and run in a consumer project with no setup beyond the package references.
Verify, mocks and VerificationGlue.Tests run under Native AOT with trimming warnings as errors.
A VerificationGlue version that differs from the one VerificationGlue.Tests was built against fails the build. Build metadata is ignored.

outcome.detail: VGT0007 build error.

scenarios.contract: Each runtime assembly carries the repository version, and the runtimes of VerificationGlue.Tests share one version.
The migration guides' after-samples build and pass.
The packages work on each SDK, framework, OS and architecture in the supported matrix.
scenarios.constraints: CI runs ubuntu-latest x64 with SDK 10.0.403 and net10.0 only.

gap.missing: Windows x64 and macOS arm64, if the gate adds them to the matrix, have no CI run.

scenarios.contract: An awaited mock result inside a rewritten assertion with short-circuiting is called once, and skipped branches stay skipped.

gap.missing: No test combines the three factors.

scenarios.contract: A constructor mock, a container-created SUT and a test parameter of the same type share identity as the resolution contract says.

gap.missing: The sample covers class scope only. No case at test or assembly scope.

scenarios.contract: A failed Check, a throwing body and several cleanup failures all survive reporting, and cleanup completes.
A recursive generic async member set up in mixed styles keeps setup, returned identity and received calls consistent.
A child task, a pending verification and a background invocation follow the context isolation and recording rules together.

gap.missing: Needs the controlled scheduling from step 3.

scenarios.contract: A packed consumer with rewriting and Native AOT generates and runs in the supported configuration.

gap.missing: PackageConsumer does not turn tier 3 rewriting on, so the AOT run does not check a captured-value message.
